We need to create jsoup Document objects with various elements, attributes, namespaces, text nodes, comments, data nodes. We must test namespace handling: elements with prefix, xmlns declarations, attribute copying with invalid characters filtered. Test that fromJsoup returns doc with correct URI when location set. Test that asString returns XML string (maybe includes namespaces). Also test that copyAttributes filters invalid attribute names. Need to access private inner class methods? copyAttributes and updateNamespaces are private. Can't directly call. But can indirectly test via conversion results. We can create element with attribute "data-@invalid" that after replacement becomes "datainvalid"? Actually replaceAll("[^-a-zA-Z0-9_:.]", ""); It removes characters not allowed. Then matches pattern. So we can test attribute with illegal characters gets cleaned. Also test that xmlns declarations affect element namespaces. Implementation: Use jsoup library. Since test code, we can use org.jsoup.Jsoup, org.jsoup.nodes.Document, Element, etc. Create a jsoup Document via Jsoup.parse("", "http://example.com") but better to build manually. . After conversion, attribute key should be "databad"? Actually original key "data-@bad": replaceAll removes characters not allowed. The hyphen is allowed, @ not allowed, so becomes "data-bad"? The regex removes any char not in allowed set, so '@' removed, resulting "data-bad". That matches pattern? "data-bad" starts with letter, contains hyphen allowed. So we can assert attribute present with key "data-bad". Also attribute "valid" remains. Test 4: fromJsoup throws NPE when null. Test 5: asString returns XML string containing root element. Also test that convert respects document location. Implementation details: Use JUnit 4: @Test, @Before. Potentially need to import needed classes. Edge Cases: Need to ensure that W3CBuilder correctly sets root and child. Also test that DataNode becomes Text node. Create jsoup Document with DataNode: e.g., element.appendChild(new DataNode("data", "")). But jsoup DataNode is part of org.jsoup.nodes.DataNode. Use element.appendChild(new DataNode("raw", "")). Check resulting W3C document has a text node child of that element. Test that comment node is converted. Implementation steps: Write test class W3CDomTest with several @Test methods. Use helper method to convert and then query via DOM APIs: doc.getDocumentElement(), getElementsByTagNameNS, etc. For namespace, need to use doc.getElementsByTagNameNS("http://example.com/ns", "ns:child")? Actually tag name includes prefix? In DOM, getElementsByTagNameNS(namespaceURI, localName). Use localName "child". So find child element and assert namespaceURI. Also test that root element's namespace is correct (should be same as declared). Test attribute cleaning: after conversion, root element attributes should include "data-bad" with value "val" and "valid" with "ok". Use getAttribute. Testing asString: Convert doc to string, ensure it contains expected XML snippet. Now craft the file with proper package? The class under test is org.jsoup.helper.W3CDom, so test class can be in same package or separate. Use package org.jsoup.helper; to access package-private? The inner class is protected static, but we don't need direct access. We'll create test class in same package to avoid import issues. Add imports for JUnit: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, org.junit.Assert.*. Now produce output with markers.
